entry.title: Mawali (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that in the 18th century the Mawali tribe (pictured) was driven from the Syrian steppe to the regions of Hama and Idlib, where their descendants live today?

entry.title: Ceechynaa (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a reviewer identified an "audible contempt" for men in the songs of Ceechynaa, who entered the UK singles chart earlier this month with "Peggy"?

entry.title: vitamin E (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that vitamin E was named "tocopherol" as it was identified as essential for live births in rats?

entry.title: Michel Klein (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that in the 1950s Michel Klein opened one of the first veterinary practices in Paris?

entry.title: puff-puff (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the sexual onomatopoeia puff-puff was censored in English releases of Dragon Quest until Dragon Quest XI?

entry.title: Jacob Frolich (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that newspaper publisher Jacob Frolich built trapdoors and hiding places in his house in case it was raided by Radical Republicans?

entry.title: Chernobyl Reactors 5 and 6 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that nearly 300 construction workers showed up at 8 am to continue building Chernobyl Reactors 5 and 6, unaware of the Chernobyl disaster earlier that day?

entry.title: Bernard Gray (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that war correspondent Bernard Gray was killed while travelling as an unofficial passenger aboard a Royal Navy submarine during the Second World War?

entry.title: Good Gravy! (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Good Gravy!, a Thanksgiving dinner–themed roller coaster, was first tested with a train full of plush turkeys?
